Glucocorticoid response in human airway smooth muscle cells: RNA-seq differential expression

Jennifer Hsieh, PhD

2026-10-10

This report summarises outputs generated by the scripts in R/. Re-run Rscript R/run_all.R to regenerate every number and figure.

1. Question

Which genes respond to the synthetic glucocorticoid dexamethasone in primary human airway smooth muscle (ASM) cells, and does the response recover known glucocorticoid biology? Glucocorticoids are the mainstay anti-inflammatory therapy in asthma, and ASM is one of their target tissues.

2. Data

  • Study: Himes BE et al. (2014) RNA-Seq transcriptome profiling identifies CRISPLD2 as a glucocorticoid responsive gene that modulates cytokine function in airway smooth muscle cells. PLoS ONE 9(6): e99625. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0099625
  • GEO accession: GSE52778, 16 samples: four primary ASM donor cell lines, each untreated, 1 µM dexamethasone, 1 µM albuterol, or both (18 h).
  • Counts: NCBI GEO RNA-seq pipeline raw gene counts (GRCh38.p13, NCBI Gene IDs), 16,802 genes tested after filtering in the primary comparison.
  • Annotation: org.Hs.eg.db (Entrez ID to symbol, name and gene type).

3. Quality control (all 16 samples)

Assigned reads per library ranged from 19.2 to 39.1 million, with 15,791-17,116 genes at ≥ 10 counts. DESeq2 median-of-ratios size factors ranged from 0.71 to 1.33. No library was an outlier on depth or detected genes.

PCA on the variance-stabilised data (top 500 variable genes) separates samples into two groups along PC1 (40.3% of variance), while PC2 (27.5%) and PC3 largely reflect the donor cell line.

Metadata check

PC1 should correspond to glucocorticoid exposure. All four untreated and all four dexamethasone samples fall where expected, but for donors N052611 and N080611 the sample annotated “Albuterol” clusters with dexamethasone-treated samples and the sample annotated “Albuterol_Dexamethasone” clusters with untreated samples. A score built from seven canonical glucocorticoid targets confirms this:

Sample Donor Annotated treatment GC score
N61311_Alb N61311 Albuterol -1.78
N61311_Alb_Dex N61311 Albuterol_Dexamethasone 1.87
N052611_Alb N052611 Albuterol 1.64
N052611_Alb_Dex N052611 Albuterol_Dexamethasone -0.46
N080611_Alb N080611 Albuterol 0.77
N080611_Alb_Dex N080611 Albuterol_Dexamethasone -1.14
N061011_Alb N061011 Albuterol -1.65
N061011_Alb_Dex N061011 Albuterol_Dexamethasone 1.95

The pattern is consistent with swapped or mis-annotated albuterol samples in those two donors (the “Albuterol_Dexamethasone” samples also show a weaker, intermediate glucocorticoid signature). This analysis does not try to resolve it. The albuterol arms are excluded, and the primary comparison uses only the untreated and dexamethasone samples, whose labels are internally consistent. These are the same eight samples distributed in the Bioconductor airway package.

4. Differential expression: dexamethasone vs untreated

Design: ~ cell_line + treatment (paired by donor), 8 samples. Genes were kept with ≥ 10 counts in ≥ 4 samples. DESeq2 Wald test, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR. Log2 fold changes were shrunk with the normal prior for the MA plot and ranking. edgeR (quasi-likelihood F-test) and limma-voom were fitted with the same design as cross-checks.

Method concordance

6. Interpretation

  • Dexamethasone produces a large, highly reproducible transcriptional response in ASM cells: 4,743 genes at FDR < 0.05, of which 1,071 change more than two-fold, roughly balanced between induction and repression.
  • The strongest hits recover canonical glucocorticoid-receptor targets: FKBP5 (GR co-chaperone and negative-feedback regulator), TSC22D3/GILZ and DUSP1/MKP-1 (both key mediators of glucocorticoid anti-inflammatory action), PER1, KLF15 and ZBTB16. CRISPLD2, the gene highlighted by the original study, is induced about 6.2-fold, which reproduces the published finding.
  • Repressed genes include the adhesion molecule VCAM1 and modest decreases in the inflammatory cytokine genes IL6 (log2FC -0.81, FDR 0.015) and CCL2 (log2FC -0.54, FDR 0.038), consistent with the anti-inflammatory profile of glucocorticoids. Up-regulated genes are enriched for extracellular-matrix organisation, cell-substrate adhesion and response to hormone stimulus, and down-regulated genes for GPCR signalling and cell-projection morphogenesis terms. These suggest effects on ASM structure and signalling beyond inflammation.
  • DESeq2, edgeR and limma-voom agree closely (Spearman ρ ≈ 0.998 for fold changes; 4,628 genes significant in all three), so the conclusions do not depend on the choice of method.

7. Limitations

  • n = 4 donors per group. The paired design controls donor effects, but inter-individual variation in response (e.g. N080611) is only partly captured.
  • A single dose and time point (18 h). Primary vs secondary response genes cannot be separated.
  • GO over-representation depends on the significance and fold-change cut-offs and on GO annotation bias; it is hypothesis-generating.
  • The albuterol and combination arms were not analysed because of the metadata inconsistency described in Section 3.
